discovery: Prediction and discovery of Bose-Einstein condensation of excitons (interlayer phase coherence) in bilayer two-dimensional electron systems

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

subfield: Condensed matter physics (mesoscopic and low-dimensional many-body physics)
motivation: MacDonald and Girvin, with collaborators, predicted that closely spaced two-dimensional electron layers at total filling factor one condense into a state with spontaneous interlayer phase coherence, equivalent to a Bose-Einstein condensate of excitons with superfluid properties. Eisenstein, using exceptionally clean double-quantum-well GaAs heterostructures and ingenious independent-contacting techniques, confirmed this with a giant Josephson-like peak in interlayer tunnelling, quantized Hall drag and vanishing counterflow resistance, demonstrating dissipationless exciton transport. This was the first unambiguous excitonic condensate in a solid, realising a decades-old idea of Keldysh, Lozovik and Blatt. It rests on precision sample design and measurement integrity, and it launched an international effort on electron-hole bilayers, Coulomb drag and, now, exciton condensates in graphene and transition-metal dichalcogenide double layers. It is a landmark of emergent many-body quantum coherence in engineered matter.
